sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 1m
facts: Official metadata exposes WCS, WMS and WMTS access
Native coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700
Published vertical accuracy is ±15 cm RMSE
Coverage period recorded as 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022
sources.limit: Composite coverage mixes survey dates and the RMSE is not a parcel-specific confidence interval

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 2m
facts: Official metadata exposes a 2 m WCS service
Native coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700
Published vertical accuracy is ±15 cm RMSE
Coverage period recorded as 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022
sources.limit: The 2 m surface is a sensitivity check and cannot replace the pinned 1 m result

sources.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
facts: Native coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700
Published vertical accuracy is ±15 cm RMSE
Dataset period extends to 18 April 2024
OSGM02-to-OSGM15 adjustment grid is supplied
sources.limit: Historic tiles require explicit survey-date and geoid handling before comparison

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model 10m
facts: Official 10 m composite DTM archive is available
Native coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700
Published vertical accuracy is ±15 cm RMSE
Coverage period recorded as 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022
sources.limit: The 10 m product is too coarse for primary sub-metre parcel measurement

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset
facts: Shows indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties
Downloads are organised by local authority
Each polygon has a unique INSPIRE ID
Polygons may occur in more than one authority package
sources.limit: INSPIRE polygons are indicative and are not legal title plans

sources.name: INSPIRE current monthly download
facts: Current dataset was published 5 July 2026
New files are published on the first Sunday of each month
Local-authority downloads are provided
Use is governed by Open Government Licence conditions
sources.limit: The package must be revalidated after the next monthly publication

sources.name: Technical guidance for GML files
facts: Source polygons are captured against British National Grid
Native CRS is EPSG:27700
Reprojection is required for common web-map coordinate systems
BNG-to-WGS84 conversion can shift features by up to 15 m
sources.limit: Exact containment and raster sampling must remain in native EPSG:27700

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 documentation
facts: Open height dataset for Great Britain
Product is updated annually in July
Grid uses regular 50 m post spacing
Data is supplied in 10 km by 10 km National Grid tiles
sources.limit: The product is landscape-scale and cannot confirm sub-metre parcel spans

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 technical specification
facts: OS Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution DTM
Buildings and trees are removed from the ground surface
Grid has regular 50 m post spacing
Grid and contours are supplied by 10 km tile
sources.limit: A specification does not prove the correctness of a particular downloaded sample

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 overview and accuracy
facts: Grid data was compared with GPS points in sample areas
Published grid accuracy is 4 m RMSE
Accuracy assessment covers urban, rural and mountain or moorland categories
sources.limit: Four-metre RMSE supports gross-outlier screening only

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data specification
facts: ASCII data is supplied beside GML metadata
Each raster row contains 200 pixels
Each pixel is 50 m by 50 m
Height values are calculated from pixel centres
sources.limit: Current archive headers and bytes still require direct hash and structure verification

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 metadata specification
facts: Per-tile XML metadata follows GEMINI conventions
Metadata identifies spatial representation
The 10 km tile reference is recorded
National Grid reference context is supplied
sources.limit: Metadata cannot replace hashes of the archive and raster payload

sources.name: Web Coverage Service standard
facts: WCS provides Internet access to multidimensional coverages
Core requirements are mandatory for conformant implementations
Encoding, CRS, scaling and interpolation are extension concerns
WCS 2.0.1 is listed as an official core standard
sources.limit: Standards text does not prove that a specific endpoint returned correct parcel values

sources.name: WCS 2.0.1 executable test suite
facts: The suite references WCS Core and its corrigendum
KVP binding requirements are included
CRS conformance is checked separately
GetCapabilities, DescribeCoverage and GetCoverage behaviours are tested
sources.limit: The generic suite is not evidence that the Environment Agency endpoint was certified by it
